subject: maths
question: P and Q together can complete a work in 30 days. Q and R together can complete the same work in 37.5 days. R and P together can complete the same work in 150 days. In how many days can all the three complete the same work while working together?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(30, 37.5, 150) = 150 units.

Efficiencies: (P + Q) = 5, (Q + R) = 4, (R + P) = 1.

Total efficiency of 2 × (P + Q + R) = 5 + 4 + 1 = 10 units/day.

Efficiency of (P + Q + R) = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 units/day.

Required time = 150 ÷ 5 = 30 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P and Q together = 30 days

Time taken by Q and R together = 37.5 days

Time taken by R and P together = 150 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Time × Efficiency

⇒ Total efficiency of 2 × (P + Q + R) = 5 + 4 + 1 = 10

⇒ Efficiency of (P + Q + R) = 10 ÷ 2 = 5

⇒ Time taken by P, Q, and R together = 150 ÷ 5 = 30 days

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Individual Work Formula

If the combined efficiency of A, B, and C is E, and A + B = E₁, then C's efficiency is E − E₁.

Time and Efficiency Relation

Time taken to complete a job is inversely proportional to the efficiency. If the efficiency ratio is A:B, then the time ratio is B:A.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the direct ratio of the total work done by each individual. If they work for the same number of days, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.
